script.text: Good morning! I'm Kelly, and this is your daily lesson for April 26. Today we're exploring two powerful ideas together.

An engine isn't magic—it's a converter.  It takes energy locked in fuel and transforms it into motion.  Whether burning gasoline or boiling water, engines do one job: convert one form of energy into another.

Most engines work by heating something—gas, steam, air—which expands and pushes. The expansion creates motion. Car engines burn fuel, steam engines boil water, jet engines compress and burn air. Heat becomes push. The steam engine, refined in the 1700s, powered the Industrial Revolution.  Factories no longer needed rivers for water power.
Today's wisdom: Here's today's wisdom: Transformation is the key to usefulness.  Engines teach that raw energy must be converted to serve purposes—and conversion always has costs.
Now let's take what we learned and put it into practice.
Today's growth challenge is Energy Conversion - Notice Transformations.

Here's your activity: Identify three 'engines' you used today—devices that convert energy from one form to another. What goes in? What comes out? What's lost? Your car, your heater, even your body. Everything useful involves conversion. This helps you see engines as energy converters.
And here's how today's lessons connect: What you learned about what engines actually do can be applied to energy conversion - notice transformations. Practice makes progress.
That's today's lesson. Learn something, grow a little. I'll see you tomorrow with something new. Stay curious!
